correctness.rationale: For the all-n one-stage formula, D-conjugation removes each site coordinate, while principal minors of the canonical lower-one/upper-q matrix equal (1-q)^(k-1), yielding the exact characteristic coefficients. Universal two-site isospectrality forces k(d)k(L-d)=Q; three-site determinant invariance forces k(a)k(b)k(c) constant on a connected simplex, and C1 differentiation gives log k affine. For two-stage Erlang, geometric winding summation gives k2(d), and qa(a+L)=a^2 yields det M2=-b^2 q w1w2 d(L-d); the positive Perron root is strictly maximal at L/2. A standalone rational-arithmetic checker confirms 54 representative identities; infinite conclusions rely on the written proof.

value.rationale: Point-to-point dispersal and geometric placement affect viability benchmarks for idealized marine networks. This theorem shows an exact degeneracy in which no geometric design can change the linear invasion multiplier, characterizes the only positive differentiable kernel with that degeneracy from natural minimal small-network tests, and demonstrates that a single extra larval travel stage yields a strict antipodal optimum and an opposite-sign secondary eigenmode. This cleanly separates kernel-shape effects from topology/patch strengths and identifies when geometry-based inference needs features beyond a memoryless point approximation. The claim is confined to the specified physical proxy.
